question_and_hypotheses.question: Does path-balanced cumulative evidence remove duplicate-path anchoring while retaining cross-boundary source recovery?

measurement_mapping.integrity: Verify deterministic chronology, no inferred relevance, identical terminal validation, no repository effect, exact ancestry, no reruns, and shared-stop behavior.

acceptance_and_scope.exposure: Same exposed eight-task cohort with three repetitions per arm. Rounds 20 and 21 remain immutable evidence. Reserved confirmation remains untouched.
acceptance_and_scope.stopping_rules: No task, threshold, scorer, branch order, context/output/total-token cap, source refresh, within-round tuning, or favorable rerun. Only the selected path-balanced state treatment changes; dual terminal envelopes and the 30-second local secret deadline are common instruments.

retained_counterevidence: Across Rounds 20 and 21, combined scheduled span gain was +0.0429065152, below +0.05.
Combined scheduled file gain was +0.0256944444, but Round 21 file gain was -0.0555555556.
Valid state completions were 38 versus 41 control across the two rounds.
Task effects were heterogeneous: C, Rust, and TypeScript were positive while Go and C++ were negative.
373 of 602 presented evidence entries duplicated a path within the same state presentation.
All actual dispatched state prompts had exactly one presentation; earlier missingness was a measurement error.
One Round 21 state terminal response remained protocol-invalid after two corrections, and one local no-dispatch secret timeout was retained.
State used 257,450 fewer cumulative branch model tokens across the two rounds.
Native context selection does not establish repair correctness, semantic use, transfer, confirmation, or clearance.
successor_rule: Freeze and run every Round 22 identity once after offline criteria pass. A development pass advances to untouched confirmation under the fixed contract. Any failed criterion closes Round 22, preserves all evidence, and requires a reviewed successor hypothesis under policy v4.
